name: Kolvex FilterMask FM-12 Urban Half-Face
description: A matte charcoal thermoplastic half-face mask covering nose to chin, manufactured by Kolvex with the same utilitarian honesty as their transit-grade filtration caps. The mask body has a slight anatomical curve and sits flush against the face via a dual-strap silicone seal. Two replaceable hex-cartridge filters flank the exhalation valve — cartridges are color-coded: grey for particulate, amber for chemical, red for biological. The exterior is stamped with the Kolvex hexagon mark in debossed relief.
functionality: Filters PM2.5 particulate, low-concentration industrial solvents, and common urban aerosols. Cartridges rated for 80 hours of use. Strap system adjusts for most head sizes including those with neck-level chrome augmentation.
what_it_says: You take the air quality seriously but you're not trying to make a statement about it.
worn_by: small business owners near industrial zones
manufacturer: Kolvex (corponation, transit and safety equipment division)
story_hooks: A batch of FM-12s sold in Circuit Ward 7 had amber cartridges that tested positive for a rare neurotoxin — whether contamination or sabotage is unresolved.
The silicone seal leaves a faint ring on the face after long wear — a visible mark that Circuit workers recognize and Spire residents find unsettling.
Someone has been swapping used red bio-cartridges back into sealed packaging and reselling them; the next outbreak could trace back to a single counterfeit shipment.

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian half-face respirator with industrial minimalism—covers nose to chin, leaving eyes and forehead exposed. The matte charcoal surface has a subtle anatomical curve that follows facial geometry. Presents as functional street-wear, neither threatening nor medical, striking a balance between safety equipment and urban fashion statement.
physical_description.fit: Compression-fitted via dual adjustable silicone straps that anchor at temple and jaw. Sits flush against facial contours with minimal gap. Tight enough for seal integrity, loose enough for all-day wear without pressure marks.
physical_description.primary_material: Matte charcoal thermoplastic (injection-molded) body with medical-grade silicone seal components and hex-threaded aluminum cartridge ports.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, hard thermoplastic face with subtle debossed hexagon logo. Silicone straps have slight grip texture. Cartridge filters have fine mesh screening visible at intake.
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte charcoal grey as primary. Accent colors on swappable cartridges: grey (particulate), amber (chemical), red (biological). Straps are dark charcoal with minimal contrast stitching.
physical_description.closures: Dual silicone elastomer straps with friction-fit adjustment (no buckles or velcro). Hex-threaded cartridge ports allow tool-free swap via hand-tight engagement.
distinctive_features: Debossed Kolvex hexagon mark on left cheek panel
Dual asymmetric filter cartridge ports with color-coded cartridges
Exhalation valve centered below mouth area
Silicone dual-strap system with temple and jaw anchors
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3–4 functional crossover. Mass-produced by major corpo division, affordable for working class, common in transit/industrial labor but increasingly adopted as street-wear aesthetic.
physical_description.cultural_context: Signals practical survivalism without subcultural affiliation. Worn by transit workers, environmental activists, street-level corpo employees, and urban dwellers in high-pollution zones. Also adopted by style-conscious Tier 3–4 residents as marker of 'honest utility' ethos. Not medical (those are full-face), not military (no comms integration).
physical_description.condition_typical: Usually pristine to lightly worn when new. With age: silicone straps show slight discoloration, minor scratches on thermoplastic body, cartridge ports accumulate dust, possible replacement cartridges indicate heavy use.
